observation_summary: The NumericEntityUnescaper throws a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when processing numeric entities that are either at the end of the string or lack a terminating semicolon, because the code assumes the existence of a semicolon without verifying the bounds of the input string.
hypothesis: The root cause is a missing boundary check in the while loop (line 54) of NumericEntityUnescaper.java. The code attempts to access input.charAt(end) to check for a semicolon without verifying if 'end' is still within the bounds of the input string, leading to an out-of-bounds access when the entity is unfinished or at the end of the input.
prediction: The fix will involve adding a condition to the while loop at line 54 to ensure 'end' is less than 'input.length()' before calling input.charAt(end).
experiment_rationale: The stack trace explicitly points to StringIndexOutOfBoundsException at line 54 (input.charAt(end) != ';'). The code logic assumes that a semicolon will eventually be found, but fails to handle cases where the string ends before a semicolon is encountered.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a classic missing boundary check. The procedure (parsing a numeric entity) is logically sound for well-formed entities, but it lacks the necessary guard to prevent an out-of-bounds access when the input string ends prematurely. This fits the definition of 'Checking' perfectly.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the loop logic is part of the algorithm, the specific failure is a missing guard/boundary check, which is the hallmark of a Checking defect.
